bullets.title: GOOGL's $80B equity raise signals AI capex now constrained by market appetite
bullets.body: Alphabet filed to offer up to 150M Series A depositary shares in an ~$80B capital raise (including a $10B Berkshire Hathaway private placement and $40B ATM offering), sending shares down ~2.7% premarket. Fintwit commentary notes this is a 'big moment for the industry' — hyperscaler spending limits are shifting from internal cash flows and bond issuance to market capacity constraints, reflecting escalating AI compute investment requirements.

bullets.title: MRVL surges 20-26% after Jensen Huang 'trillion dollar company' call at Computex
bullets.body: Marvell jumped 20-26% premarket after NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang called it the 'next trillion dollar company' at the Computex keynote. Separately, Marvell's own CEO Matt Murphy highlighted that connectivity — not compute or memory — is the next AI infrastructure bottleneck, with copackaged optics positioned as the critical enabling technology.

bullets.title: HPE +26% premarket on strong AI-driven results and raised guidance
bullets.body: HPE surged 26% premarket on strong AI-driven results and increased guidance, cited alongside MRVL and GOOGL as the key premarket movers in the AI infrastructure complex.

bullets.title: S&P 500 +20% rally since March is 'insanely narrow' — just 10 stocks drove 68% of gains
bullets.body: The S&P 500 has surged 20% since end of March, but commentary flags the rally as 'insanely narrow,' with just 10 stocks accounting for 68% of the advance. Passive indexing flows are concentrating in mega-cap names, raising index concentration risk.

bullets.title: WSTS revises global semiconductor market forecast to $1.51T in 2026, up 90%
bullets.body: WSTS sharply raised its global semiconductor market forecast to $1.51 trillion in 2026, up 90% from current levels and well above the March estimate of $1.0T. Memory alone is expected to surge +250% to over $800B; logic up 37%; Americas region up 112%. Global semis projected to reach $1.9T in 2027.

bullets.title: South Korean semiconductor exports to U.S. surge 671.5% YoY
bullets.body: South Korean semiconductor exports to the U.S. increased 671.5% year-over-year, corroborating the broader AI-driven chip demand surge and consistent with WSTS's bullish memory market revision.

bullets.title: CBOE dispersion index at 3rd highest ever — market pricing major single-stock divergence
bullets.body: CBOE DSPX (dispersion index) is at its 3rd highest reading in history, surpassed only by the April 2025 tariff shock and COVID in 2020. The index measures the ratio of S&P 500 index implied vol to single-stock IV, signaling the market is pricing significant divergence between broad index and individual stock moves.

bullets.title: AI rally showing vulnerability — Barclays and rising cost concerns
bullets.body: Barclays warns the AI-driven stock rally is 'becoming increasingly vulnerable' due to investor euphoria, crowded positioning, and rising interest-rate risks, even as strong earnings and AI optimism provide support. Separately, a Bloomberg-cited piece flags rising AI infrastructure costs as a potential threat to S&P 500 record run by pressuring corporate margins.

bullets.title: AI is power-bound, not compute-bound — grid/nuclear names flagged as next leg
bullets.body: Fintwit commentary emphasizes that Jensen Huang and Elon Musk have been saying for a year that AI is power-constrained, not compute-constrained, yet investor positioning remains skewed toward chip names. Names highlighted as beneficiaries include CEG (largest U.S. nuclear operator, 32GW, hyperscaler PPAs signed), VST (nuclear fleet, major AI data center deals in Texas), TLN (sold 960MW campus to Amazon for $650M), and SMR (only fully NRC-approved SMR design).

bullets.title: NAND shortage to persist through Q4 2027 — Kioxia seeking hyperscaler LTAs through 2029+
bullets.body: Kioxia's Investor Day flagged that the supply-demand curve for NAND will only gradually recover and the shortage is projected to remain through Q4 2027. Kioxia is simultaneously seeking long-term NAND supply agreements with hyperscale data centers extending through 2029 and beyond.

bullets.title: SK Hynix plans to double memory wafer capacity; AI shortages seen through 2030
bullets.body: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won stated AI-driven memory shortages could persist through 2030, while SK Hynix is preparing to double its wafer capacity over five years. Memory prices — more than logic chips — drove the bulk of the recent semiconductor growth surge.

bullets.title: Tech was the only S&P 500 sector to outperform the index in May; IGV sees record retail buying
bullets.body: Technology drove all S&P 500 returns in May and was the sole sector to outperform the broad index. Separately, retail investors recorded their largest-ever single-session purchase of IGV (software ETF), signaling sustained retail conviction in the AI/software theme.

bullets.title: ISM Manufacturing hits four-year high in May; construction spending beats
bullets.body: The ISM Manufacturing Index reached a four-year high in May as new orders expanded for the fifth consecutive month, with 16 industries reporting growth — the most since April 2022. Separately, April construction spending rose +0.4% m/m vs. +0.2% estimate, with private residential up +0.8%.

bullets.title: ECB considering June 'insurance hike' as euro area CPI hits 3.2%
bullets.body: ECB's Rehn described a potential June rate move as an 'insurance hike' against inflation risks, while Simkus stressed the importance of timely reaction. Euro area preliminary May CPI came in at 3.2% YoY, in line with estimates.

bullets.title: JPMorgan raises CrowdStrike PT to $800 from $475, maintains Overweight
bullets.body: JPMorgan significantly raised its price target on CrowdStrike to $800 from $475 while maintaining an Overweight rating, a 68% PT increase signaling strong conviction in the cybersecurity name.

bullets.title: Elon forecasts 90% of distance driven will be autonomous within 10 years
bullets.body: Elon Musk stated '10 years from now, probably 90% of all distance driven will be autonomous,' a bullish forward-looking comment for Tesla's FSD program. Tesla is also reporting strong vehicle registration growth across European markets in May.

bullets.title: META expands teen safety controls globally across Instagram, Facebook, and Messenger
bullets.body: Meta is rolling out 13+ content settings for teen accounts globally on Instagram and extending the 'Limited Content Setting' to Facebook and Messenger later this year. The move reflects ongoing regulatory and reputational pressure around youth safety on social platforms.

bullets.title: U.S. large-cap ETFs lead inflows for another consecutive week
bullets.body: U.S. large-cap ETFs continued to dominate with the largest inflows for yet another week in the period ending 5/29/26, while global ETFs led outflows — consistent with ongoing domestic concentration of capital flows into mega-cap U.S. equities.

bullets.title: MicroStrategy reportedly planning bitcoin sales to maintain solvency — contradicts Saylor's hodl doctrine
bullets.body: WSJ reports MicroStrategy/Strategy is preparing to sell part of its bitcoin holdings to maintain solvency, directly contradicting Michael Saylor's longstanding 'never sell' public messaging.

bullets.title: Microsoft Build 2026 conference underway — watch for AI product announcements
bullets.body: Microsoft is hosting its Build 2026 developer conference, a key event for AI product announcements and Azure/Copilot updates that could drive incremental sentiment on MSFT.
